slides.source: NJ Division of Taxation (Nov. 2026); Therm, confirmed Oct 22 2026 (6 years)

slides.title: 18% of your rent
slides.body: On your NJ return, 18% of the rent you paid on your main home counts as property taxes. Deduct it, up to $15,000, or take the $50 credit. Not both.
slides.source: NJ Division of Taxation, Property Tax Deduction/Credit (updated 3/23/26)

slides.title: Up to $15,000
slides.body: Owners deduct the property taxes they actually paid on their main home, up to $15,000. Same rule: the deduction or the $50 credit, not both.
slides.source: NJ Division of Taxation, Property Tax Deduction/Credit (updated 3/23/26)

slides.label: NUMBER 3: ANCHOR
slides.body: For 2025, homeowners with income up to $150,000 could get $1,500. Renters under 65 with income up to $150,000 could get $450.

slides.title: Rent $2,500 a month?
slides.body: That's $30,000 a year. 18% of it, $5,400, counts as property taxes on your NJ return. Compare it with each home's tax bill. Talk to a tax professional.
slides.source: NJ Division of Taxation (Nov. 2026); example math

caption:
Here's what actually happens at tax time when you rent vs. own in New Jersey.

Renters: 18% of your rent counts as property taxes on your NJ return. Owners: you deduct the taxes you paid, up to $15,000. For 2025, ANCHOR paid $1,500 to homeowners with income up to $150,000 and $450 to renters under 65.

Put both in your rent vs. buy math. Talk to a tax professional about your own return.
